subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Read and write numbers up to 7 digits using Indian place value system
Compare and order large numbers using < and > symbols
section_description: Introduce students to numbers beyond 10,000, explaining the Indian numeral system including lakhs and crores with real-world examples such as population figures and distances.

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Identify properties of whole numbers: closure, commutativity, associativity
Apply distributive property to solve problems
section_description: Design a hands-on activity where students verify properties of whole numbers using number cards and grouping exercises.

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Identify and name basic geometric shapes: point, line, ray, line segment
Distinguish between open and closed curves
section_title: Concept Explanation: Points, Lines and Curves
section_description: Explain geometric concepts using real-world objects in the classroom such as corners, edges of tables and windows.

subject: Science
chapter_title: Food: Where Does It Come From?
learning_outcomes: Classify food sources as plant-based or animal-based
Identify the role of different animals and plants in our food chain
section_description: Begin with a discussion about what students ate for breakfast, then categorize those items into plant and animal sources using a class chart.

subject: Science
chapter_title: The Living Organisms and Their Surroundings
learning_outcomes: List and explain characteristics that distinguish living from non-living things
Identify habitats and explain how organisms adapt to their environment
section_description: Use classroom observations and a sorting activity with pictures of living and non-living things to help students identify key characteristics of life.

subject: Science
learning_outcomes: Identify components of a simple electric circuit
Distinguish between conductors and insulators
section_description: Introduce circuit diagrams and component symbols. Have students build a simple circuit using a battery, bulb, and wires to understand current flow.

subject: Social Science
chapter_title: The Earth in the Solar System
learning_outcomes: Name and sequence the planets in our solar system
Explain why Earth is considered the only planet capable of supporting life
section_description: Use a model or diagram of the solar system to introduce planets. Compare sizes and distances using scaled representations.

subject: Social Science
learning_outcomes: Define latitude and longitude
Locate important parallels and meridians on a globe
section_description: Explain the concept of the equator and parallel lines of latitude. Have students practice locating the Tropic of Cancer, Tropic of Capricorn, and polar circles.

subject: English
learning_outcomes: Identify characters and their contrasting traits
Infer the moral of the story from events
section_description: Guide students to compare the two birds through a Venn diagram activity, discussing how environment shapes behavior and values.

subject: Hindi
learning_outcomes: कविता के भाव और भाषा को समझना
प्रकृति के प्रति कवि के भाव की पहचान करना
section_description: कविता को पढ़कर उसमें वर्णित चिड़िया की विशेषताओं और कवि के प्रकृति-प्रेम को समझाएं।

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Understand the need for negative numbers in real life
Perform addition and subtraction of integers using number line
section_description: Use contexts such as temperature below zero, debt, and floors below ground level to introduce negative integers. Practice on a number line.

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Identify and measure complementary and supplementary angles
Apply properties of angles formed by a transversal with parallel lines
section_description: Demonstrate angle pairs using folded paper and protractors. Guide students to discover the sum properties of complementary and supplementary angle pairs.

subject: Science
learning_outcomes: Explain the process of photosynthesis with the chemical equation
Identify the raw materials and products of photosynthesis
section_description: Use a diagram of a leaf cross-section to explain chlorophyll and light absorption. Include a simple experiment with a green leaf and starch testing using iodine solution.

subject: Science
learning_outcomes: Distinguish between conduction, convection, and radiation
Give everyday examples of heat transfer in each mode
section_description: Demonstrate heat transfer through a metal rod (conduction), hot water rising in a beaker (convection), and sunlight warming skin (radiation). Students categorize daily examples.

subject: Social Science
chapter_title: Tracing Changes Through a Thousand Years
learning_outcomes: Explain how historical sources help us understand the medieval period
Identify key changes in political and social structure between 700-1750 CE
section_description: Use a timeline and primary source images to introduce the medieval period. Discuss how scholars write history from coins, inscriptions, and manuscripts.

subject: Social Science
learning_outcomes: Identify the rise of regional powers after the decline of the Gupta Empire
Explain the role of land grants in spreading power among regional rulers
section_description: Map activity showing the emergence of Rashtrakutas, Palas, and Gurjara-Pratiharas. Analyze a sample land grant inscription to understand political structures.

subject: English
learning_outcomes: Identify the central moral of the story
Discuss how the three questions relate to decision-making in real life
section_title: Discussion: The Moral of the Story
section_description: Facilitate a Socratic seminar where students discuss the answers to the three questions and connect them to situations in their own lives.

subject: Hindi
learning_outcomes: गद्यांश के मुख्य भाव को समझना
दादी माँ के चरित्र की विशेषताओं को पहचानना
section_description: पाठ में दादी माँ के व्यक्तित्व का विश्लेषण करते हुए उनके स्नेह, त्याग और बुद्धिमत्ता के उदाहरण छात्रों से खोजवाएं।

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Represent rational numbers on a number line
Perform all four operations on rational numbers
section_description: Guided practice on adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing fractions and negative fractions. Use visual models (fraction strips) before abstract practice.

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Solve linear equations with variables on both sides
Apply linear equations to solve word problems
section_description: Present age, money, and distance problems that require setting up and solving linear equations. Students work in pairs and present solutions.

subject: Science
learning_outcomes: Classify microorganisms into bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa, and algae
Explain the role of useful microorganisms in food preparation and medicine
section_description: Use labeled diagrams and a comparison table to classify microorganisms. Show examples from daily life: yeast in bread, bacteria in curd, Penicillium in antibiotics.

subject: Science
learning_outcomes: Define combustion and identify conditions necessary for it
Distinguish between rapid, spontaneous, and explosive combustion
section_description: Demonstrate burning of a candle, magnesium ribbon, and phosphorus (or video) to show different combustion types. Students record observations and classify each.

subject: Social Science
learning_outcomes: Define resources and classify them as natural, human, and human-made
Explain sustainable use of resources
section_title: Types of Resources and Sustainable Use
section_description: Use a resource audit of the classroom to classify what students see. Discuss sustainable practices through a case study of rainwater harvesting or solar energy.

subject: Social Science
learning_outcomes: Classify industries by ownership, raw material, and scale
Explain factors that influence the location of industries
section_description: Case study of a steel plant (Tata Steel, Jamshedpur) to analyze how proximity to raw materials, transport, and labor affect industrial location.

subject: English
chapter_title: The Best Christmas Present in the World
learning_outcomes: Analyze character motivation and feelings
Understand the impact of war on human relationships
section_description: Students analyze Jim's letter from the trenches and discuss what it reveals about his character, hopes, and the reality of war through close reading questions.

subject: English
learning_outcomes: Identify cause-and-effect relationships in an informational text
Appreciate animal instincts as described in the text
section_description: Graphic organizer activity: students trace the sequence of events that led to survivors escaping the tsunami, identifying causes and their effects.

subject: Hindi
learning_outcomes: कहानी की मुख्य घटनाओं का क्रमबद्ध वर्णन करना
मशीनीकरण के कारण पारंपरिक शिल्पों पर पड़ने वाले प्रभाव को समझना
section_title: कहानी का सारांश और सामाजिक सन्देश
section_description: कहानी के माध्यम से छात्रों को पारंपरिक शिल्पकारों की समस्याओं और आधुनिकीकरण के प्रभाव पर विचार करने के लिए प्रेरित करें।

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Define irrational numbers and give examples
Locate irrational numbers on the number line using geometric construction
section_title: Irrational Numbers on the Number Line
section_description: Demonstrate how to construct √2 on the number line using a compass and ruler. Students practice constructing other surds and verify they cannot be expressed as fractions.

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Classify polynomials by degree and number of terms
Apply Factor Theorem to find factors of a polynomial
section_description: State and prove the Factor Theorem with examples. Guide students through factorizing quadratic and cubic polynomials using the theorem and long division.

subject: Science
learning_outcomes: Describe the states of matter in terms of particle arrangement
Explain processes of interconversion of states with examples
section_description: Use particle-level diagrams to compare solids, liquids, and gases. Demonstrate sublimation of camphor and evaporation of acetone to show state changes.

subject: Science
learning_outcomes: State Dalton's Atomic Theory and its postulates
Calculate molecular mass and mole concept for simple compounds
section_title: Dalton's Atomic Theory and Molecular Mass
section_description: Present Dalton's postulates and discuss evidence supporting them. Practice calculating molecular masses of H₂O, CO₂, and NaCl using atomic masses.

subject: Science
learning_outcomes: Classify plant tissues as meristematic and permanent
Identify and describe simple permanent tissues: parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma
section_description: Observe prepared slides or diagrams of plant tissues. Students fill a comparison table identifying location, cell structure, and function for each tissue type.

subject: Social Science
learning_outcomes: Identify the social, political, and economic causes of the French Revolution
Explain the significance of the Declaration of the Rights of Man
section_description: Present the three estates system using a visual. Students analyze primary source excerpts from pamphlets of the period to identify grievances of the Third Estate.

subject: Social Science
learning_outcomes: Explain how colonial policies transformed forest management in India
Describe the impact of commercialization of forests on tribal communities
section_title: Colonial Forest Policies and Their Impact
section_description: Case study comparing pre-colonial and colonial forest use. Students analyze a map of reserved forests in India and discuss the displacement of Adivasi communities.

subject: English
learning_outcomes: Predict how technology will shape future education
Compare the fictional school of the future with present-day schooling
section_description: Students debate whether digital learning is better or worse than classroom learning, connecting ideas from the story to their own experiences with technology.

subject: Hindi
learning_outcomes: पाठ के माध्यम से स्वतंत्रता के महत्व को समझना
हीरा और मोती के चरित्र के माध्यम से मित्रता और सहयोग के मूल्यों को पहचानना
section_description: हीरा और मोती की विशेषताओं की तुलनात्मक तालिका बनाकर छात्रों को दोनों के व्यक्तित्व और आपसी संबंध को विश्लेषित करने का अवसर दें।

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: State and apply Euclid's Division Lemma
Find HCF of numbers using Euclid's Division Algorithm
section_title: Euclid's Division Algorithm: Concept and Application
section_description: Demonstrate the algorithm with concrete examples (HCF of 135 and 225). Students practice in pairs and verify results using prime factorization.

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Identify quadratic equations in standard form
Solve quadratic equations by factorization and quadratic formula
section_description: Compare three methods (factorization, completing the square, quadratic formula) with the same equation. Students decide which method is most efficient for different equation types.

subject: Science
learning_outcomes: Write balanced chemical equations for given reactions
Classify chemical reactions: combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement
section_description: Step-by-step balancing of equations using hit-and-trial method. Students practice balancing 8 equations of increasing difficulty and classify each reaction type.

subject: Science
learning_outcomes: Describe the process of nutrition in human beings including digestion, absorption, and assimilation
Trace the path of food from mouth to small intestine
section_description: Use a labeled diagram of the human digestive system. Students trace food journey, noting enzymes and organs at each stage with a flow chart activity.

subject: Science
learning_outcomes: Explain Mendel's experiments with pea plants
Define dominant and recessive traits and predict offspring ratios using Punnett squares
section_description: Walk through Mendel's monohybrid cross experiment. Students use Punnett squares to predict outcomes for seed color and seed shape crosses.

subject: Social Science
learning_outcomes: Identify the main events of the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22)
Explain why Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922
section_description: Timeline activity covering key events from 1920-22. Students analyze a primary source excerpt from Gandhi's writings on Chauri Chaura to understand why the movement was suspended.

subject: Social Science
learning_outcomes: Explain why power sharing is important in a democracy
Distinguish between horizontal and vertical power sharing with examples
section_description: Case comparison: Belgium's power sharing model vs. Sri Lanka's majoritarian approach. Students evaluate outcomes and discuss which model promotes stability.

subject: English
learning_outcomes: Analyze the theme of faith and trust in God
Identify irony in the story and explain its effect on the reader
section_description: Close reading activity focusing on Lencho's faith. Students identify ironic moments in the story and discuss how irony creates meaning and tone.

subject: Hindi
learning_outcomes: पाठ में परिवारिक संबंधों की जटिलता को समझना
बड़े भाई के संस्कारों और छोटे भाई की स्वतंत्र सोच में अंतर देखना
section_description: बड़े भाई के कठोर अनुशासन और छोटे भाई के लापरवाह रवैए के बीच संघर्ष को नाटक के रूप में प्रस्तुत करने की गतिविधि।

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Define sets and describe methods of representing sets
Perform union, intersection, and complement operations on sets
section_description: Use Venn diagrams to visualize union, intersection, and complement. Students solve problems involving real-world data organized into sets (e.g., students in clubs).

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Distinguish between mathematically acceptable and unacceptable statements
Identify and construct converse, inverse, and contrapositive of conditional statements
section_description: Present examples of open and closed statements. Students classify statements and practice writing converses of conditional statements from textbook examples.

subject: Physics
learning_outcomes: Explain the principle of dimensional analysis
Use dimensional analysis to check correctness of equations and derive formulas
section_title: Dimensional Analysis: Checking and Deriving Formulas
section_description: Demonstrate dimensional analysis for kinematic equations. Students check three physics formulas for dimensional correctness and derive the formula for time period of a simple pendulum.

subject: Physics
learning_outcomes: State Newton's three laws of motion with examples
Apply Newton's second law to solve force-mass-acceleration problems
section_title: Newton's Laws: Demonstrations and Problem Solving
section_description: Demonstrate each law with classroom activities (coin-card flip, push-pull, action-reaction). Students solve tiered problems applying F = ma to single objects and systems.

subject: Chemistry
learning_outcomes: Calculate atomic mass and molecular mass for compounds
Explain the mole concept and apply it to calculate number of particles
section_description: Introduce mole as a counting unit using analogies (dozen, gross). Students calculate molar mass of compounds and convert between moles, mass, and number of particles.

subject: Biology
learning_outcomes: Explain the need for classification and the concept of species
Describe the hierarchical classification system from Kingdom to Species
section_description: Use a familiar organism (mango, dog) to trace the full taxonomical hierarchy. Students classify five organisms and discuss why standardized nomenclature is essential.

subject: English
learning_outcomes: Analyze the theme of generation gap and changing traditions
Describe the narrator's relationship with his grandmother at different life stages
section_description: Students create a life-stage diagram of the grandmother and discuss how the narrator's relationship with her changes and what this reveals about modernization and tradition.

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Define and classify functions as one-one, onto, and bijective
Find inverse of a bijective function and verify
section_title: Types of Functions and Inverse Functions
section_description: Graphical and algebraic identification of function types. Students test functions for injectivity and surjectivity and find inverses for simple bijective functions.

subject: Mathematics
learning_outcomes: Apply integration by substitution to evaluate indefinite integrals
Recognize when substitution simplifies an integral
section_title: Integration by Substitution: Technique and Practice
section_description: Demonstrate substitution method with 3 worked examples of increasing complexity. Students practice 10 integrals, identifying appropriate substitution in each case.

subject: Physics
learning_outcomes: State Coulomb's law and calculate electrostatic force between charges
Apply superposition principle to systems of multiple charges
section_description: Derive Coulomb's law formula and compare it with Newton's gravitational law. Students solve problems involving force between two and three charges using vector addition.

subject: Physics
learning_outcomes: Explain Young's Double Slit Experiment and derive fringe width formula
Calculate fringe width and angular fringe width for given parameters
section_description: Step-by-step derivation of fringe width formula. Students solve 5 problems calculating fringe width, wavelength, and slit separation using the derived formula.

subject: Chemistry
learning_outcomes: Define molarity, molality, mole fraction, and mass percentage
Calculate concentration in different units for given solutions
section_description: Compare concentration units with real-world examples (saline, alcohol solutions). Students convert between concentration units and solve problems on preparation of standard solutions.

subject: Chemistry
learning_outcomes: Distinguish between electrolytic and galvanic cells with diagrams
Calculate EMF of a cell using standard electrode potentials
section_description: Draw and explain a Daniell cell diagram. Students calculate EMF for given half-cell reactions and determine spontaneity using the sign of EMF.

subject: Biology
learning_outcomes: Compare asexual and sexual reproduction in terms of mechanisms and advantages
Describe types of asexual reproduction with examples from plants and animals
section_description: Gallery walk with labeled diagrams of binary fission, budding, fragmentation, and vegetative propagation. Students match each type to examples and explain advantages.

subject: English
learning_outcomes: Analyze the use of symbolism in the story
Interpret the themes of language, identity, and patriotism in the context of French-Prussian war
section_title: Symbolism and Themes in The Last Lesson
section_description: Students identify symbolic elements (the pigeons, the primer, M. Hamel's clothing) and discuss how each symbolizes aspects of cultural identity and loss.
